claims.text: Multi-objective optimization algorithms can concurrently improve the strength and ductility of metals and alloys.
Multi-objective optimization can improve strength and ductility by optimizing microstructural properties.
Multi-objective optimization algorithms can be applied to design and optimize material microstructures.
Grain size and precipitate distribution are the structural mediators affected by the optimization.
Optimizing grain size and precipitate distribution can balance strength and ductility.
The optimized material will exhibit a 10% increase in strength relative to material produced by traditional alloy-design methods.
The optimized material will exhibit a 15% increase in ductility relative to material produced by traditional alloy-design methods.
Relationships between microstructural properties and material behavior are not fully understood.
Computational models may not fully capture real-world material behavior.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts 10% strength and 15% ductility increases, but the rule only falsifies it below 5% strength or 10% ductility. Results between those thresholds and the predicted values would fail to meet the stated prediction without falsifying it.
